chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sends blessings upon the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) while he is in the obligatory prayer, either bowing or prostrating, so he sends blessings upon him while he is in that state. He said: 'Yes, indeed, sending blessings upon the Prophet of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) is like the form of the Takbir and the Tasbih, and it is ten good deeds that eighteen angels compete to deliver to him.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to send blessings upon the Prophet during the bowing or prostration of obligatory prayer?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, affirming that sending blessings during the physical postures of Ruku' and Sajdah is legally valid, treating it akin to the essential ritual formulas of Takbir and Tasbih. The narration highlights the immense spiritual merit of this act, noting that it yields ten good deeds which eighteen angels compete to deliver to the Prophet, underscoring the continuous connection between the worshipper and the Prophet even within the strictures of the obligatory prayer.
